en.about: Custom Versification Editor is a Paratext tool for a project's custom.vrs, the file that says how the project's chapter and verse numbering differs from its standard versification. Add chapters with a different number of verses, map verses to the standard versification, and list verses the translation leaves out, without typing the file by hand. Each entry can be turned off without deleting it.

en.title: Custom Versification Editor
en.sub: A Paratext tool: change a project's verse numbering, without editing the file by hand
en.text: Custom Versification Editor is a Paratext tool. It edits a project's custom.vrs, the file that says how the project's chapter and verse numbering differs from its standard versification. You don't have to type the file by hand.

en.title: Open it from the Tools menu
en.q: How do I open Custom Versification Editor?
en.text: In Paratext, open the project. Then choose {0}Tools, then {1}Custom Versification Editor.

en.title: It opens your project's custom.vrs
en.text: The editor opens your project's custom.vrs. {0}At the top are the project and its standard versification. {1}The yellow bar reminds you to restart Paratext after saving. {2}There are three kinds of entries, each on its own tab. {3}This project already has one: Revelation 12 has 17 verses.

en.title: A chapter with a different number of verses
en.q: How do I give a chapter a different number of verses?
en.text: In many Spanish Bibles, Third John has 15 verses instead of 14. To record that, choose {0}the book, type {1}the chapter {2}and its last verse, {3}then click Accept.

en.title: Added in Bible order
en.q: How do I turn an entry off without deleting it?
en.text: {0}The entry is added, and the list is kept in Bible order. {1}Tick Disabled to turn an entry off without deleting it. It stays in the file as a comment, and Paratext ignores it.

en.title: Map a verse
en.q: How do I map a verse to the standard versification?
en.text: On the Mapping tab, you link a verse of the project to a verse of the standard versification. Here, {0}the project's verse 15 {1}goes with verse 14. {2}Click Accept. For a range, fill in the small box after the verse as well.

en.title: The mapping is listed
en.q: Where do I see the mappings?
en.text: {0}The mapping is listed. To remove an entry, select it and click Delete.

en.title: A verse the translation leaves out
en.q: How do I list a missing verse?
en.text: On the Missing Verses tab, list the verses that are not in the translation, for example Matthew 17, verse 21. {0}Fill in the book, chapter and verse. {1}To add several verses in a row, fill in the last one here. {2}Click Accept.

en.title: Each missing verse on its own line
en.q: Why is each missing verse listed separately?
en.text: {0}Each missing verse is listed on its own, as custom.vrs requires. {1}Here too, Disabled turns an entry off.

en.title: Save custom.vrs
en.text: {0}Choose File, then Save. The changes are saved in the project's custom.vrs. If the project had no custom.vrs yet, saving creates it.

en.title: Restart Paratext
en.q: Why doesn't Paratext show my changes yet?
en.text: {0}The status bar shows the file and how many entries it has. {1}Paratext reads custom.vrs only when it starts. So close Paratext and open it again to use the new numbering.

en.title: Installing the tool
en.q: How do I install the tool?

en.title: Ready to use
en.text: Start Paratext again. {1,0}Custom Versification Editor is now on the Tools menu.

en.title: Custom Versification Editor
en.sub: Chapters, mappings and missing verses  ·  Turn entries off without deleting them  ·  Restart Paratext after saving
en.text: Custom Versification Editor records how your project's numbering differs from its standard versification: chapters with a different number of verses, mappings, and missing verses. Remember to restart Paratext after you save.
